name: cloud-tasks
description: Diego's Cloud Tasks (formerly Cloud Agenda, before that Cloud Calendar) — standalone Android task, calendar and event app. The applicationId stays com.diegonmarcos.cloudagenda so installed phones update in place. Jetpack Compose chrome (CloudKitTheme light/dark/system, libs:bottomnav island + page tabs, a page-managed hamburger drawer, AI and Profile buttons in the top row, libs:ai chat with persistent history) over a local tasks database (projects > lists > tasks > subtasks, statuses, tags, links to Cloud Mail / Cloud Drive items) and a mail agent that proposes tasks for review. The Feeds page is still the legacy tasks.html WebView (public-ICS feed sync, CalDAV against a self-hosted Radicale). Build via Nix devShell, one APK out.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps. KEY LOCATION: Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/signing.secrets.yaml.

libs:clock-tools._doc: #1668 Tasks > Clock: the fleet's one clock, shared BY REFERENCE with Cloud Calc and the SuperApp (FullClock: World clock, Alarms, Timers, Stopwatch, Interval, Bedtime). Its manifest merges the clock's service, receivers, ring screen and permissions (notifications and exact_alarm are in perms.needs). Alarms set here live in THIS app's own store and ring from this app only. No host meta-data: the lib's ClockConfig.DEFAULT (Cloud Calc's declared numbers) and this app's launch activity. A `gui` lib.

libs:clock-tools-core._doc: #1668 the clock's rules (plain JVM), the api of libs:clock-tools; its suite runs in this app's `gradle test` (mutation-tested in Cloud Calc's).

libs:perms._doc: #1360 the permission contract (libs:perms): Configs > General > Perms (AppPermsSection, linked by libs:ui-nav-bars), first run (PermsFirstRun), PermsGate, and the state provider helper apps are read through.

libs:theme-background._doc: #1157 shared navigation and theme design, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:ui-kit._doc: The Compose kit: CloudKitTheme and the palette roles every page paints with, the settings rows, chips, segmented picks and banners. Shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:ai._doc_dir: The AI dropdown: the fleet's AI chat (libs:ai) over the fleet agent gateway (my-ai-api, mesh only), sessions kept in the app's files dir so the history is permanent. Shared BY REFERENCE. This app holds no OpenRouter token and reads none (decisions-use guard D5): the gateway holds the fleet key. Its mesh address is baked as BuildConfig.AI_GATEWAY_URL by libs/ai/ai-gateway.gradle. The mail agent's extraction calls the same gateway.

libs:model-catalogue._doc_dir: libs:ai's `api` dependency: the shared agent descriptor (assets/agents/agents.json) its Agent picker and the Agent settings page list. Listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

engines._doc: ENGINES THIS APP BINDS INSTEAD OF COMPILING (engine-apk-split F2; same shape as ac_cloud-me/build.json::engines). `fleet` is the Store row in aa_cloud-superapp/data/constellation-fleet.json from which app/build.gradle resolves the package (an unknown id fails the build) for BuildConfig and <queries> -- without the query Android 11+ hides the engine and CalBridge read it as not installed; `action` finds the service in it ({package} substituted at build time, matching the engine manifest's ${applicationId}.ENGINE); `min_contract` is the lowest engine CONTRACT that answers every method CalBridge calls, read through PackageManager BEFORE binding. Cloud Me binds the same engine: one calendar cache, one task mirror.

auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.

analytics._doc: Consumed by :libs:analytics, which reads THIS file (rootDir) at build time and bakes the values into BuildConfig. Both backends are single-site today, so every app reports into the same site and is told apart by .app — give each app its own site_id once per-app sites exist in Umami/Matomo.

ui._doc: #868 THE navigation declaration (libs:bottomnav NavDecl): ui.bottom_nav is the island's ids, ui.sections the section each one opens, ui.default_section where the app opens. #1456 the island is Inboxes | Backlogs | Tasks | Library | Projects. The four collection sections list their items in the Cloud Me Tasks row layout from the mock fixture (assets/mock-tasks.json, FAKE data); Tasks has the sub-pages Calendar, List (the native database list with the projects drawer), Gantt, Kanban, Mindmap and (#1668) Clock: the full clock of libs:clock-tools (World clock with the #1667 converter and day bars, Alarms, Timers, Stopwatch, Interval, Bedtime), the same lib Cloud Calc and the SuperApp carry. Settings is NOT on the island: it opens from the top bar's Settings > Configs and follows the fleet Configs pattern, General | Perms | About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs) first, then the app's own Appearance, Agent, Proposals (mail-agent review) and Feeds. Every section's `background` is `theme`.

top_bar._doc: THE first row of the app (libs:bottomnav AppTopBar, declared once for the fleet): a hamburger that opens a side drawer the CURRENT page fills (the Tasks page: the projects and their lists; Calendar and Settings: their pages), the title, and two circular buttons: AI (libs:ai's chat in an anchored panel, one box for search and chat, history kept) and Settings (Account launches Cloud Account; Configs opens the Settings section: Appearance, Agent, Inbox, Feeds). No app draws its own copy of this row (cloud-android-top-bar-guard).

tests._doc: Read by 1_cicd/dist/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh, which the ship workflow runs before it builds. shell = the static testers under test/ (the declared navigation and its Kotlin ids; the screenshot parser). unit = gradle test: the data model, migrations, seeding, filter logic and the mail agent's parsing as JVM tests, and the Robolectric Compose layout-tree tests of the chrome (drawer, top row, filter bar, task editor).

shell._doc_requires: test-agents-parser.sh runs the screenshot parser under node; a missing tool must fail the preflight rather than draw a verdict from its own absence.

configs_pages._doc: Configs > General and Configs > About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs, rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json, #1352 v2). general.sections: the anchors of the one General page, in order (perms, battery, storage, notifications, ui, language are required; app opens this app's own Configs; update is added after perms by default). about: the hand-written part of the extensive About: tagline, description, features, screens, guide, privacy, backends (ids of ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints, resolved to mesh URLs at build time), related fleet apps, credits for a fork. Permissions, data stores, crash/analytics libs, name, icon, version, build sha and date, repo, licence, origin, crash sink, debug API and changelog are derived, never typed here.

about.tagline: What is due, when it happens, who is invited
about.description: Cloud Tasks (formerly Cloud Agenda) is the fleet's task, calendar and event app: task lists, a calendar with events, and invites, with the AI gateway helping to turn a sentence into a task. The package name stays the old one so installed phones update in place. It exists so the owner's schedule lives in one app backed up with the phone profile.
features: Turn a sentence into a task with AI

screens.name: Calendar
screens.what: Events by day, week and month.

guide: Add a task with the plus button.
Switch to Calendar to plan the week.
about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. Usage analytics are opt-in and off by default; when allowed, events go only to the owner's self-hosted Umami and Matomo. It talks only to the fleet services listed below, over the private mesh first.

perms._doc: #1360 every grant this app needs, by libs:perms catalogue id (needs), and the fleet apps that do work for it with the grants THEY must hold (helpers). The ONE declaration: generated into assets/app-perms.json (cloud-android-perms-guard.py --write), drawn by Configs > General > Perms (libs:perms AppPermsSection) with live state, Grant / Open and Grant all, asked at first run (first_run), and reported as 'Missing permission X - Grant' when an operation fails (PermsGate). perms-guard fails when code uses a gated API or another app's engine that is not declared here, or when the manifest and this list disagree.
